question.problem: What is the limit of the sequence ${a}_{n}=\frac{(2{n}^{2}+3)(2{n}^{2}-3)}{2n(5{n}^{3}-1)}$ for $n\ge 1?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we multiply out the numerator and denominator of the sequence and get

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{(2{n}^{2}+3)(2{n}^{2}-3)}{2n(5{n}^{3}-1)}=\frac{4{n}^{4}-9}{10{n}^{4}-2n}.
$$

So to find the limit, we will need to compute

$$
{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n}={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{4{n}^{4}-9}{10{n}^{4}-2n}.
$$

The dominant term in the denominator is $10{n}^{4},$ so we divide the numerator and the denominator by ${n}^{4}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{4{n}^{4}-9}{10{n}^{4}-2n} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{4{n}^{4}}{{n}^{4}}-\frac{9}{{n}^{4}})}{(\frac{10{n}^{4}}{{n}^{4}}-\frac{2n}{{n}^{4}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(4-\frac{9}{{n}^{4}})}{(10-\frac{2}{{n}^{3}})} \\  & =\frac{4-0}{10-0} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the sequence converges and its limit is $\frac{2}{5}.$
